    20→## Regulatory pathway

    22→| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical timeline |

    28→| DDI (dead/diseased/imminent hazard) heritage tree | Administrative variance still required, but no fee and 0% mitigation — City Arborist letter (not private arborist alone) determines DDI | City Arborist + Director | ~1–2 months |
    29→| LOC > 25 acres OR any LOC in Barton Springs Zone | Phased ESC plan required (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a; LDC § 25-8-184); BSZ adds 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap | DSD Environmental | Within site plan cycle |

    31→| Karst feature (cave, sinkhole, fault, fracture) over EARZ | 50-ft walking transect karst survey by Texas Licensed Professional Geoscientist (ECM 1.10.3); 150–300 ft buffer to catchment | WPD | Adds 1–3 months |

    33→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (within 1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Pkwy) | Native tree replacement (LDC § 25-2-1022) + 40% natural-area set-aside (LDC § 25-2-1025) | DSD | Constrains massing from concept stage |
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→**Tree inventory and survey**
    38→- All trees ≥ 8" DBH must be surveyed by an RPLS within 5 years of submittal (ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A). Off-site and ROW trees count if their CRZ reaches the LOC — a 30-inch tree 28 ft beyond the boundary still triggers survey because its 30-ft CRZ enters the site (ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
    39→- Heritage trees (≥ 24" DBH + listed species) must be marked "H"; protected trees (≥ 19" DBH any species) annotated. Multi-trunk DBH formula: largest stem + ½ each additional stem ≥ 1" (ECM 3.3.2.A.2).
    40→- For initial diligence, satellite imagery is not a substitute — DBH cannot be inferred from canopy and field survey is the precondition to any reliable site plan. Budget RPLS + ISA-certified arborist field work before committing to massing.
    41→
    42→**Critical Root Zone (CRZ) geometry — the buildable envelope killer**
    43→- CRZ radius (ft) = DBH (in); Half CRZ = DBH ÷ 2 ft; Quarter CRZ = DBH ÷ 4 ft (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). For a 30" heritage oak: 30-ft CRZ, 15-ft Half CRZ, 7.5-ft Quarter CRZ.
    44→- Three nested rules apply simultaneously: ≥ 50% of total CRZ area preserved at natural grade with natural ground cover; cut/fill ≤ 4" in the Half CRZ; **zero cut/fill of any depth in the Quarter CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Failing any of the three means the tree is legally "removed" — mitigation and variance triggered whether or not the developer intends removal.
    45→- "Construction impacts" are measured at the line of excavation, not the visible face of improvements — over-excavation behind curbs, scaffolding, concrete form bracing, staging, and utility trenching all count (ECM 3.5.2.A.3). A curb shown right at the Half-CRZ line is non-compliant.
    46→- City Arborist may (discretionary, not automatic) require an enlarged CRZ at 1¼ to 1½ × standard radius for Post Oak (*Quercus stellata*), rare trees, or trees in sensitive conditions (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Assume the larger radius for Post Oak when massing.
    47→
    48→**Heritage tree removal**
    49→- Removal prohibited without a permit; permit only issues with an approved variance under LDC § 25-8-642 (admin, < 30" stem) or § 25-8-643 (LUC + EC, ≥ 30" stem). Tree must meet one of the five § 25-8-624(A) criteria: prevents reasonable access, prevents reasonable use, imminent hazard, dead, or diseased and not restorable.
    50→- Prerequisite-variance rule (LDC § 25-8-646): applicant must have first sought and been denied every other applicable Code variance, waiver, exemption, or alternative compliance (setbacks, AEC, compatibility, etc.) before requesting heritage removal. This adds calendar time and forces concept-stage exploration of layout alternatives.
    51→- Mitigation: standard heritage rate is **300% of removed caliper inches** (ECM 3.5.4.A.1); reduced 150% rate is City-Arborist-discretionary for verified poor condition; DDI is 0% (City Arborist determination required). 19"+ protected tree (Appendix F species) is 100%; non-Appendix F 19"+ is 50%; 8–18.9" is 50%/25%.
    52→- Three mitigation forms (ECM 3.5.4.B): on-site replanting, preserved-undersized-tree inch-for-inch credit, or fee-in-lieu to the Urban Forest Replenishment Fund (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch (private) — but UFRF is only available when the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for planting. ROW/parkland trees route to the Planting for the Future Trust (PFTF), tracked separately.
    53→- Replacement trees: at least 75% of total caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species (Appendix F "SS" column — 39 species).
    54→
    55→**Erosion and sedimentation control (ESC)**
    56→- Every site requires an ESC plan (LDC § 25-8-181; ECM § 1.4). The Limit of Construction (LOC) is the operative boundary and must encompass all disturbance including off-site work and staging; ESC quantities (silt fence, mulch sock) are computed from actual LOC and disturbed area (ECM 1.4.4.B.3).
    57→- Phasing trigger: LOC > 25 acres requires a phased ESC plan (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a). **Any site in the Barton Springs Zone requires phasing regardless of LOC size**, plus the 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap (LDC § 25-8-184; ECM Appendix P-3).
    58→- Default plan scale is 1"=50' (Environmental Review Requirements § 3); 1"=100' only with express DSD authorization for large sites.
    59→- Cut/fill > 4 ft must be disclosed for Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural, and BSZ sites; Urban watersheds are exempt.
    60→- Silt fence: J-hooks at 100-ft intervals, individual sections ≤ 200 ft (ECM 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.1 / 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.4). Triangular Filter Dikes allowed only in sheet flow (≈ first 100 ft of flow path); concentrated flow areas need rock berms (ECM 1.4.5.H).
    61→- Stabilized construction entrance: 4–8" open-graded crushed stone, ≥ 8" thick, ≥ 50 ft long, full ingress/egress width (ECM 1.4.5.N; SSM 641S).
    62→
    63→**Environmental zones and CEFs**
    64→- Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) along any waterway with ≥ 64-ac drainage area (LDC § 25-8-92). Widths vary by watershed class: urban watersheds = 100-yr fully developed floodplain; suburban = 100/200/300 ft by waterway size; water supply / BSZ = floodplain-based with min/max from centerline. CWQZ within LOC requires hatching and native grassland seeding per Spec 609S.6.
    65→- CEFs (LDC § 25-8-1(6)): bluffs, canyon rimrocks, caves, faults/fractures, seeps, sinkholes, springs, wetlands. Standard 150-ft three-dimensional buffer (LDC § 25-8-281(C)). Karst point-recharge features over EARZ extend to topographic catchment (150–300 ft); wetland buffer measured from outer delineation edge.
    66→- Save Our Springs (BSZ) impervious cover caps: 15% recharge zone, 20% contributing zone within Barton Creek watershed, 25% remainder. **No variance or waiver available** (LDC § 25-8-515); only the pre-1991 small-lot exemption (≤ 8,000 SF total IC) or Chapter 245/HB 1704 vested-rights determination provides relief. Plan to design under the cap from day one.
    67→- Slope > 15% anywhere on site triggers ERI requirement and slope-stabilization design (LDC § 25-8-121(B)).
    68→
    69→**Vegetation removal and landscape compliance**
    70→- Removal permit required for every regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) including the 15 mitigation-exempt invasive species (Arizona Ash, Chinaberry, Chinese Parasol, Chinese Pistache, Chinese Tallow, Koelreuteria, Ligustrum, Mimosa, Paper Mulberry, White Mulberry, Photinia, Salt Cedar, Siberian Elm, Tree of Heaven, Vitex) — no mitigation but the permit is still required (ECM 3.5.4.A.2.b).
    71→- Excessive pruning (> 25% foliage in an annual growing season) is statutorily defined as removal (LDC § 25-8-602(4)(d); ECM 3.5.2.A.2). Scaffolding clearance pruning counts toward the 25% — if a building can't be built without exceeding it, the building must move.
    72→- Landscape plan + parking lot / street tree requirements under LDC § 25-2-1001 and ECM Section 2; SCM plantings (biofiltration, rain gardens) bridge with `sde` and have their own native-species and buffer rules.
    73→
    74→**Hill Country Roadway Corridor (if applicable)**
    75→- Native tree replacement under LDC § 25-2-1022 for each removed native (live oak, Spanish oak, cedar elm, shin oak, bald cypress, post oak, pecan, bur oak, black walnut), small native, or cluster of 3+ native trees 2–6" within 10 ft.
    76→- Small natives subject to replacement: Texas madrone, black cherry, Texas mountain laurel, evergreen sumac, Mexican buckeye, flameleaf sumac, Texas persimmon.
    77→- 40% of site in natural state (LDC § 25-2-1025). Check "Hill Country Roadways Overlay" in facts.md — applies only inside the corridor, not to general BSZ/EARZ sites.
    78→
    79→**Tree protection physical detailing (constructability)**
    80→- Chain-link fence ≥ 5 ft tall at or beyond the CRZ boundary; trunk wrap (2×4 lumber wired, first 8 ft of trunk, retightened every 6 months) required when fence is within 5 ft of trunk (ECM 3.6.1; SSM 610.4.A).
    81→- Mulch ≥ 8" deep in any unfenced section of CRZ; no material storage within fenced CRZ.
    82→- Boring pits within CRZ must be ≥ 4 ft below existing grade; bore pits within Half CRZ are flagged as a deficiency (ECM 3.5.2.B.2).
    83→- All work within CRZ by hand; small equipment only with 8" mulch + plywood/mats (ECM 3.6.1.C.2–3).
    84→
    85→**BSZ-specific non-degradation and operating requirements**
    86→- BSZ sites must demonstrate zero-net-increase in annual average loadings for 10 regulated pollutants (LDC § 25-8-514(A)) via SLAT, ECM 1.6.9.3 manual equations, or independent engineering analysis.
    87→- Two SCMs in series required (ECM 1.6.9.3): first retention-type, second volume-reduction-type — design implication for site plan layout and elevations from concept.
    88→- Commercial and multifamily BSZ projects require annual water-quality operating permit (LDC § 25-8-233); ECM 1.2.2.1 standard cover-sheet block required.
    89→- BSZ redevelopment > 25 dwelling units requires City Council approval after EC review (LDC § 25-8-26(F)(1)) — significant political/calendar risk.
    90→
    91→## Opportunities to evaluate
    92→
    93→- **DDI pathway**: if the City Arborist determines a heritage or protected tree is dead, diseased, or an imminent hazard, removal is no-fee and 0% mitigation. Private arborist reports alone do not establish DDI — pursue the City Arborist letter early when condition is genuinely poor.
    94→- **150% poor-condition rate** for heritage trees: City-Arborist-discretionary halving of the 300% mitigation if a qualified arborist documents poor condition and the City Arborist approves. Worth pursuing on declining heritage oaks.
    95→- **Modified CRZ (MCRZ)** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.b): City Arborist may reconfigure CRZ boundary when prior development blocked root growth, as long as total area equals standard CRZ and it stays inside the protection fence. Half/Quarter CRZ rules still apply.
    96→- **Like-for-like existing impacts** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a): rebuilding within the footprint of existing Half- or Quarter-CRZ impacts is allowable if no deeper or wider — useful on infill with existing slabs/curbs within CRZ.
    97→- **Elevated foundations within Half CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.B.3): allowed with ≥ 4" air gap, natural-grade soil beneath, non-leaching barrier for concrete; cannot span the Quarter CRZ; footprint still counts toward the 50% impact ceiling.
    98→- **Low-impact excavation** (ECM 3.5.2.B.2): hand digging or compressed-air ("air spade") permitted in restricted zones; significant roots (≥ 1.5" diameter) cannot be cut without City Arborist authorization.
    99→- **Transplant** (ECM 3.5.2.B.5): City-Arborist-discretionary alternative to removal; requires qualified large-tree transplant arborist, fiscal surety, and 5-year hold before release.
   100→- **Fee-in-lieu** (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch private, **$75/caliper inch for certified affordable developments** — meaningful savings on dense affordable projects, but only available when site is "unsuitable for planting" per City Arborist.
   101→- **Wetland buffer 1:1 mitigation** (ECM 1.10.4(D)(3)): standard 150-ft wetland buffer can be reduced to 50-ft average via on-site in-kind mitigation — not an admin variance, a separate pathway.
   102→- **ERI waiver** (LDC § 25-8-121(E), Form ECM 1.3.2 to wpderi@austintexas.gov): available before application; never granted if any wetland is on or within 150 ft.
   103→- **AEC for landscape only** (ECM § 2.5.0): Alternative Equivalent Compliance for LDC § 25-2-1001 landscape requirements (Director of Planning). Does **not** apply to environmental requirements — don't conflate with CEF or SOS relief.
   104→
   105→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   106→
   107→- **environmental.md** — CWQZ delineation, watershed classification (urban/suburban/water supply/BSZ), EARZ status, mapped CEFs and wetlands within 150 ft, slope analysis with any >15% area, Hill Country Roadway Corridor flag
   108→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed LOC, building footprints, parking, grading limits, utility runs, drives; any tree symbology on concept plans (usually approximate)
   109→- **zoning-pathway.md** — overlays that trigger additional tree rules (HCRC, Waterfront, BSZ), compatibility and setback constraints (drive prerequisite-variance analysis)
   110→- **arborist field survey (if any)** — RPLS-certified survey with DBH, species, multi-stem stems, condition rating; otherwise flag as data gap requiring field work before site plan
   111→- **aerial imagery + historic** — identify trees that may have appeared (now > 8") or been removed without permit since last survey
   112→- **City Arborist Addendum (if any prior submittal)** — any enlarged-CRZ directives, prior MCRZ approvals, DDI letters
   113→
   114→## Output structure
   115→
   116→Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Order findings: (1) heritage-tree CRZ conflicts with proposed footprint, (2) protected-tree removal exposure and mitigation cost band, (3) ESC phasing / scale / cut-fill compliance, (4) CEF and CWQZ buffer impacts, (5) SOS impervious-cover headroom (BSZ only), (6) HCRC native-replacement and 40% natural-area set-aside, (7) landscape and replacement-tree caliper budget, (8) data gaps requiring field survey.
   117→
   118→## Severity heuristics
   119→
   120→| Finding | Severity |
   121→|---|---|
   122→| Heritage tree CRZ or Quarter CRZ overlaps proposed building footprint with no like-for-like existing impact | `significant` — likely LUC variance (if any stem ≥ 30") or admin variance + 300% mitigation; reshape massing |
   123→| Heritage tree Half CRZ overlaps proposed impervious; >4" cut/fill required | `moderate` — workable via elevated foundation, MCRZ, or hardship review; quantify mitigation if reclassified as removal |
   124→| Multiple protected trees (19"+) in proposed parking area | `moderate` — 100%/50% mitigation cost; consider angled parking or layout shift |
   125→| Site in Barton Springs Zone with proposed impervious approaching or exceeding 15/20/25% SOS cap | `significant` — no variance pathway; redesign required unless small-lot or HB 1704 vested |
   126→| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | `significant` — 150-ft buffer compresses envelope; ERI waiver unavailable; 1:1 mitigation pathway reduces to 50-ft avg if pursued |
   127→| Slope > 15% on portions of site | `moderate` — ERI required; slope stabilization and ESC design uplift |
   128→| Karst feature suspected over EARZ | `moderate` to `significant` — Licensed Professional Geoscientist karst survey + 150–300 ft catchment buffer |
   129→| LOC > 25 ac or any LOC in BSZ — no phased ESC plan budgeted | `moderate` — schedule impact, EPM designation, 18-month BSZ revegetation cap |
   130→| Tree survey absent or > 5 years old | `data-gap` — RPLS field survey required before reliable Phase 3 findings; assume worst case in interim |
   131→| Standard erosion controls suffice (low slope, urban watershed, contained drainage, < 25 ac LOC) | `note` |
   132→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor applies (≤ 1,000 ft of one of the 5 corridor roadways) | `moderate` — 40% natural-area set-aside is a hard massing constraint; native-replacement cost |
   133→| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" proposed for any impact that would reclassify as removal | `significant` — LUC + EC hearing track adds 4–8 months and public risk |
   134→
   135→## Common pitfalls
   136→
   137→- Inferring heritage status from canopy in aerial imagery — DBH at 4.5 ft above natural grade is the only valid measure; field survey by RPLS is the precondition.
   138→- Treating only the building footprint as the impact line — Austin measures impacts at the line of excavation, which extends behind curbs, into form bracing, and through scaffolding swing (ECM 3.5.2.A.3).
   139→- Forgetting the Quarter CRZ. The 50% rule is the famous one, but the Quarter-CRZ prohibition on any cut/fill of any depth (ECM 3.5.2.A.1) is the one that most often kills proposed sidewalks, curbs, and utility runs near heritage oaks.
   140→- Assuming a 1.5x CRZ automatically applies to Post Oaks. Enlargement is City-Arborist-discretionary and only governs if directed in writing — but assume the enlarged radius for diligence on any Post Oak.
   141→- Citing ECM 3.5.3 or Appendix P-6 — both repealed by Rule R161-22.16 (December 2022); the operative sections are ECM 3.5.2.A.2 (crown), ECM 3.5.2.A.3 (construction impacts), and ECM 3.5.2.B.1 (remedial tree care). The ECM 3.6.2 standard plan note still contains stale cross-references.
   142→- Conflating BSZ and EARZ. They overlap but are distinct: a site may be in one and not the other; SOS impervious caps key on watershed + zone combination.
   143→- Conflating ECM 2.5.0 AEC with environmental relief. AEC covers landscape (LDC § 25-2-1001) only; CEF buffers, CWQZ, SOS impervious, and wetland setbacks have their own pathways.
   144→- Counting elevated-foundation soil-preserved areas as "preserved" in the 50% CRZ calculation. ECM 3.5.2.B.3 explicitly counts them as impacts.
   145→- Underestimating prerequisite-variance time (LDC § 25-8-646). The applicant must seek and be denied every other applicable variance/waiver/AEC before requesting heritage removal — this cannot be parallelized with the heritage variance itself.
   146→- Forgetting that mitigation-exempt invasive species still require a removal permit — no mitigation fee, but the permit gate remains.
   147→- Ignoring CRZs of ROW and off-site trees that reach into the LOC. They are subject to the same 50% / Half / Quarter CRZ rules as on-site trees (ECM 3.5.2.A applied via ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
   148→- Tree survey older than 5 years. ECM 3.3.2.A invalidates surveys past 5 years from survey date; re-survey before relying on it for protected/heritage determinations.
   149→- Confusing the SOS Ordinance impervious cap with general BSZ rules. The SOS caps (LDC § 25-8-514) have no variance pathway (LDC § 25-8-515) — there is no design-around. Verify watershed + recharge/contributing zone combination at the parcel level.
   150→- Treating the Erosion Impact Zone (EIZ) around an existing building as a basis for removing a heritage or protected tree. EIZ proximity is not an approved removal criterion under LDC § 25-8-624(A).

**Severity:** data-gap

**Citation:** ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A (RPLS-certified tree survey required within 5 years of submittal for all trees >= 8" DBH on site, on adjacent property with CRZ entering the LOC, or in the adjacent ROW)

**Finding:** No tree survey has been performed for this property. The lot has been developed since 1993, providing 30+ years for trees to reach protected (>= 19" DBH) or heritage (>= 24" DBH, listed species) status. Satellite and street-level imagery cannot substitute for field measurement — DBH at 4.5 ft above natural grade is the only valid metric for regulatory classification.

**Implication for the developer:** Without a tree survey, it is impossible to determine whether any heritage or protected trees exist, whether CRZs constrain the building footprint, or what mitigation costs may apply. All massing and site plan work performed before the survey is speculative and may require wholesale revision.

**Recommended next step:** Commission an RPLS-certified tree survey with ISA-certified arborist species identification and condition rating before investing in architectural design. The survey must include trees on adjacent lots and in the ROW whose CRZ (radius in feet = DBH in inches) reaches into the LOC. Budget approximately $1,500-$3,000 for the survey on a lot this size.

---

### 2. Potential Heritage Trees — Variance and Mitigation Exposure

**Severity:** moderate

**Citation:** LDC 25-8-602(1) (heritage species list); LDC 25-8-642 (admin variance for heritage < 30" stem); LDC 25-8-643 (LUC + EC variance for >= 30" stem); ECM 3.5.4.A.1 (300% mitigation rate)

**Finding:** Heritage species common to north Austin Blackland Prairie / Scofield-era landscaping include live oak (*Quercus virginiana*), cedar elm (*Ulmus crassifolia*), and pecan (*Carya illinoinensis*) — all listed under LDC 25-8-602(1). A tree planted at subdivision development (circa 1990-1993) could now exceed 24" DBH, qualifying as a heritage tree. Removal of a heritage tree requires an administrative variance (or LUC + EC variance if any stem >= 30"), prerequisite-variance exhaustion under LDC 25-8-646, and mitigation at 300% of removed caliper inches.

**Implication for the developer:** If a 24" heritage oak must be removed, mitigation alone would cost approximately $14,400 (24" x 300% = 72 caliper inches x $200/inch fee-in-lieu) — and fee-in-lieu is only available if the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for replanting. On-site replanting of 72 caliper inches of significant shade providers is the default and requires substantial planting area. The prerequisite-variance requirement (LDC 25-8-646) adds 2-4 months of calendar time before the heritage variance can even be filed.

**Recommended next step:** Complete the tree survey (Finding 1). If heritage trees are present, engage the City Arborist early to discuss preservation alternatives, potential MCRZ approval, or DDI status if condition is poor. Design massing around heritage CRZs rather than planning for removal.

---

### 3. Protected Tree Removal Likely — Mitigation Cost to Budget

**Severity:** moderate

**Citation:** LDC 25-8-624(A) (removal criteria); ECM 3.5.4.A.1 (100% mitigation for 19"+ Appendix F species; 50% for non-Appendix F 19"+; 50%/25% for 8-18.9")

**Finding:** On a 7,840 sq ft lot where the entire existing house, driveway, and yard will be demolished and replaced with a larger duplex footprint, removal of one or more protected trees (>= 19" DBH) is probable. Even trees in the 8-18.9" range require a removal permit and mitigation (50% if Appendix F species, 25% otherwise).

**Implication for the developer:** Mitigation costs for protected (non-heritage) trees are more manageable — a 20" protected Appendix F tree would require 20 caliper inches of replacement (100% rate), or $4,000 fee-in-lieu. Multiple removals could accumulate to $5,000-$15,000 depending on inventory. At least 75% of replacement caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species.

**Recommended next step:** After the tree survey, map all regulated trees against the proposed building footprint, driveways, utility trenches, and staging areas. Optimize the site plan to preserve the largest trees and minimize mitigation obligations.

---

### 4. Critical Root Zone Constraints on Duplex Footprint

**Severity:** moderate

**Citation:** ECM 3.5.2.A.1 (CRZ radius = DBH in inches, measured in feet; 50% preservation rule; Half CRZ <= 4" cut/fill; Quarter CRZ zero disturbance); ECM 3.5.2.A.3 (impacts measured at line of excavation, not face of improvements)

**Finding:** On a small lot (7,840 sq ft), the CRZ of even a single large tree can consume a significant portion of the buildable area. A 24" tree has a 24-ft CRZ radius (1,810 sq ft circle), a 12-ft Half CRZ, and a 6-ft Quarter CRZ with zero tolerance for any cut or fill. The CRZ of trees on adjacent lots or in the Cinchring Ln ROW that extends into this lot is subject to the same rules. Austin measures construction impacts at the line of excavation — over-excavation, form bracing, scaffolding, and utility trenching all count.

**Implication for the developer:** A heritage or large protected tree near the center or front of the lot could eliminate duplex configurations that require full-width building footprints. The Quarter CRZ prohibition is absolute and frequently constrains sidewalks, curbs, and utility laterals. The City Arborist may impose an enlarged CRZ (1.25x-1.5x) for Post Oak, further compressing the envelope.

**Recommended next step:** Once the tree survey is complete, plot CRZ, Half CRZ, and Quarter CRZ circles on the site plan at the concept stage, before committing to massing. Evaluate elevated foundation options within the Half CRZ (ECM 3.5.2.B.3) and like-for-like existing impacts (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a) where the existing house slab already encroaches.

---

### 5. Erosion and Sedimentation Control — Routine Requirements

**Severity:** note

**Citation:** LDC 25-8-181; ECM 1.4 (ESC plan required for all development); ECM 1.4.4.B.3 (LOC-based quantities)

**Finding:** An ESC plan is required for demolition and construction. The site is small (0.18 ac), flat, in the Walnut Creek suburban watershed, outside the BSZ, and below all phasing thresholds (LOC < 25 ac). Standard ESC measures apply: silt fence at downslope LOC perimeter, stabilized construction entrance (>= 50 ft crushed stone pad, >= 8" thick), and inlet protection for any nearby storm drains. No phased ESC plan, no 18-month revegetation cap, and no cut/fill > 4 ft disclosure are required (urban/suburban watershed exemption).

**Implication for the developer:** ESC compliance is straightforward and should not affect project schedule or cost materially. The civil engineer will include the ESC plan on the site plan sheets at 1"=50' scale.

**Recommended next step:** Include ESC in the civil engineering scope. Ensure the stabilized construction entrance is feasible given the lot frontage and any existing street trees in the ROW.

---

### 6. Demolition-Phase Tree Protection Obligations

**Severity:** note

**Citation:** ECM 3.6.1 (tree protection fencing); SSM 610.4.A (chain-link >= 5 ft at CRZ boundary; trunk wrap within 5 ft); ECM 3.5.2.A.3 (construction impacts include staging and equipment)

**Finding:** Tree protection fencing must be installed before demolition begins — not just before new construction. Demolition equipment, debris staging, material storage, and truck access within the CRZ of any regulated tree (>= 8" DBH) constitutes a code violation and can trigger reclassification of the tree as "removed," with full mitigation consequences. The existing concrete driveway and house slab provide some protection during demolition if trees are behind the structure, but heavy equipment tracking across root zones outside the existing impervious footprint is prohibited without 8" mulch and plywood/mat protection.

**Implication for the developer:** The demolition contractor must be briefed on tree protection requirements. Demolition and tree protection plans should be coordinated — tree fencing is a precondition to the demolition permit, not a later site-plan item.

**Recommended next step:** Once the tree survey identifies regulated trees, prepare a tree protection plan that covers both the demolition and construction phases. Specify fencing locations and trunk wrap requirements in the demolition scope of work.

---

### 7. No Environmental Overlays — Favorable Regulatory Position

**Severity:** opportunity

**Citation:** Environmental research confirms: not in BSZ (LDC 25-8-481); not in EARZ (30 TAC Ch. 213); not in CWQZ; no known CEFs (LDC 25-8-281); no Hill Country Roadway Corridor; Zone X (no floodplain); no wetlands expected

**Finding:** The property is free of the environmental overlays that trigger the most burdensome tree and erosion requirements in Austin. There is no BSZ impervious cover cap, no phased ESC, no ERI requirement (no slopes > 15%, no EARZ, no wetlands within 150 ft), no karst survey, no CWQZ buffer, and no Hill Country Roadway Corridor native-tree replacement or 40% natural-area set-aside.

**Implication for the developer:** The regulatory pathway for tree protection and erosion control is limited to the standard citywide tree ordinance (LDC Ch. 25-8 Subchapter B) and standard ESC (LDC 25-8-181). This is the simplest regulatory posture available in Austin and should not introduce material schedule risk beyond the tree survey and any resulting variance proceedings.

**Recommended next step:** No action needed on environmental overlays. Focus diligence resources on the tree survey and heritage/protected tree analysis.

---

### 8. Like-for-Like Existing Impacts — Potential Opportunity

**Severity:** opportunity

**Citation:** ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a (rebuilding within footprint of existing Half- or Quarter-CRZ impacts is allowable if no deeper or wider)

**Finding:** The existing house, driveway, and concrete sewer vault have occupied portions of this lot since 1993. If any regulated trees have CRZs that overlap these existing impervious surfaces, the developer may claim like-for-like existing impacts — meaning new construction within the same footprint and depth as the existing improvements does not count as additional CRZ encroachment. This is particularly valuable on a small infill lot where the existing slab may already be within a Half or Quarter CRZ.

**Implication for the developer:** This opportunity is only quantifiable after the tree survey. If a heritage tree's CRZ overlaps the existing house slab, rebuilding within that same footprint avoids triggering the CRZ preservation rules for that area, potentially saving the project from a variance requirement.

**Recommended next step:** Document the existing house footprint, driveway, and sewer vault locations precisely (from the existing survey or demolition plan) before demolition. Overlay these against CRZs from the tree survey to identify like-for-like credit areas.

---

### 9. Landscape Replacement Requirements for New Duplex

**Severity:** note

**Citation:** LDC 25-2-1001 et seq.; ECM Section 2 (landscape and parking lot tree requirements)

**Finding:** The new duplex must comply with Austin's landscape requirements, including minimum tree plantings and landscaped area percentages. For residential development on a single lot, the requirements are less onerous than commercial or multifamily site plans, but tree replacement plantings (from any removal mitigation) count toward landscape compliance. At least 75% of replacement caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species per ECM Appendix F.

**Implication for the developer:** Landscape compliance is routine but should be coordinated with tree mitigation replanting to avoid double-counting issues. On a 7,840 sq ft lot with a duplex footprint, available planting area may be limited.

**Recommended next step:** Include landscape plan in the civil/site plan scope. Coordinate with the arborist on species selection for any mitigation replanting to satisfy both mitigation and landscape requirements simultaneously.

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Tree survey:** Has any informal tree inventory or site visit been conducted? Are there any known large trees on the lot, on adjacent lots near the property line, or in the Cinchring Ln ROW? Even informal observations (species, approximate size, location) would help scope the RPLS survey and flag likely heritage candidates.

2. **Existing site survey:** Does the existing boundary survey show tree locations or canopy outlines? The seed data references a survey (FIRM panel, easements, building line) but does not mention tree symbology.

3. **Duplex massing flexibility:** How flexible is the building footprint? If heritage trees are found, can the duplex be reconfigured (e.g., stacked units, narrower footprint, shifted placement) to avoid CRZ conflicts, or is the program fixed?

4. **Existing house footprint dimensions:** What are the precise dimensions and location of the existing house slab, driveway, and sewer vault? These are needed to evaluate like-for-like existing impact credit (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a) against any CRZ overlaps.

5. **Demolition sequencing:** Is there a preferred demolition contractor or timeline? Tree protection fencing must be in place before any demolition activity; this needs to be communicated to the demo team.

6. **Adjacent lot trees:** Are there large trees on the neighboring properties (especially to the sides and rear) whose canopies overhang or approach the property line? A tree with CRZ extending into this lot from an adjacent parcel is subject to the same protection rules as an on-site tree.

7. **Budget tolerance for mitigation:** What is the developer's budget tolerance for tree mitigation fees? Heritage tree mitigation at 300% can run $10,000-$25,000+ per tree; understanding cost sensitivity will help prioritize preservation vs. removal strategies once the survey is complete.
